about.titleHighlight: whoever maintains the code next in mind.
about.description: I like to understand the problem before writing a line: define the architecture, care about interface details and leave code the team can read, test and improve.

steps.title: I understand the problem and design the solution
steps.text: I read the requirements and the Figma, and define architecture, types and the API contract before writing code.

steps.title: I build with quality from the start
steps.text: Reusable components, strict typing, accessibility and tests as part of the work, not an afterthought.

steps.title: I optimize my flow with good tools
steps.text: I use AI assistants for refactors and repetitive tests, and verify every change against real API responses before integrating it.

steps.title: I share my decisions in code review
steps.text: I open clear, easy-to-review PRs, explain the reasoning behind each decision and discuss it with the team. I also review my teammates' PRs.

architecture.title: How I organize code
architecture.subtitle: Two patterns I apply in production: layered architecture to organize the backend, and continuous deployment to ship it with high availability.

patterns.title: Layered architecture
patterns.description: I keep business logic separate from the framework: each layer has a single responsibility, so the database or the API can change without rewriting the rules.

patterns.title: Deployment and high availability
patterns.description: Every change goes through an automated pipeline and reaches production in replicated containers, so critical platforms stay up even if a replica fails.
